correctness.rationale: The identity D_t=E^{-1}(E^{t^2}-E(q^t)^t) is exact. Iterated Frobenius lifting proves every prime-power difference is divisible by p^{a+1}. The binomial valuation v_p(C(p^{2a},j))=2a-v_p(j) isolates the first modulus-p^{a+2} nonzero difference at index p^{a-1} with residue -p^{a+1}. When t has multiple primes, at every p^a exactly dividing t, the first coefficient nonzero modulo p is at p^{2a} and equals -(t/p^a)^2. As the degree-one difference is -t^2, this determines the full gcd. All p including 2, a>=1, and all coefficient degrees are proved. Two independent exact coefficient algorithms agree over 21 parameter cases.

originality.rationale: The motivating October 2026 article establishes the t-modulus dichotomy, plus the p^2 congruence at t=p, but explicitly leaves further prime-power lifts as a possibility in Section 5. The exact p^{a+1} optimum for every a>=2 and the first obstruction at p^{a-1} are not its statements. The non-prime-power obstruction already comes from that article, but incorporating it into the exact all-parameter gcd formula is meaningful. Earlier inspected papers on eta-quotient lacunarity and coefficient congruences in progressions do not state the exact global two-series content. A classical p-adic lifting lemma accounts for the lower bound; the separate first-coefficient valuation establishes sharpness. Historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The gcd of all differences is the natural maximal uniform modulus relating two classical partition generating functions, and the source explicitly raises the possibility of lifting the prime-power congruence. The theorem gives a complete exact answer for every t, not an arbitrary truncated search: it determines p^{a+1} at every prime power and 1 at every parameter with more than one prime factor, with a canonical first sharp witness for each case. The one additional p-adic layer is structurally sharp and the exact invariant is motivated; the proof requires no claim of broader downstream consequences.
